title: Image rigidity after all supported finite-model comparisons have been supplied
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$, with discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring on profinite sets is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$, using all continuous maps. On each scheme $V$, put $\Lambda_V=p_V^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_V=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_V}$, with ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories and actual module-derived global sections to abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Use the small sites and indexing universe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention].
Let $t:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Assume that for every locally torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, without a common annihilator, the actual restriction $H^q(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)\to H^q((T_0)_{\mathrm{et}},t_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F)$ is bijective for every $q\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Choose a finite chain
$$S=T_r\xrightarrow{a_r}T_{r-1}\longrightarrow\cdots\xrightarrow{a_1}T_0'=T,$$
where each arrow is either a quasi-compact open immersion or a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $J_k=(a_k)_!$ in the open case and $J_k=(a_k)_*$ in the closed case, and put $J=J_1\circ\cdots\circ J_r$, with $J=\mathrm{id}$ for $r=0$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. The symbol $T_0'$ is only the root of this chain; the closed member of the pair is $T_0$.
For any coefficient ring $R$ mentioned below, its sheaf is $R_V=p_V^*C(-,R)$; a finite scalar local model means a module locally isomorphic to $R_V\otimes_{\underline{R}}\underline P$ for a finitely presented scalar $R$-module $P$, on a pro-étale cover. Define $\mathsf B_R(t)$ to mean: for every finite chain of the specified open and closed immersions ending in $T$, and every finite scalar local model $L$ on its source, the actual ordinary module-derived restriction
$$\rho_{R,J,L}:R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},J L[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma((T_0)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},t^*J L[0])$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. This notation is just the displayed quantified property, not an additional definition node. It includes all chains, including the identity chain, with no quasi-compactness assumption on the complement of $t$.
For the fixed coefficient $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$, assume the additional quantified property $\mathsf B_\Lambda(t)$. Let $L,M$ be finite constant scalar local models on $S$, on possibly different pro-étale covers, and let $u:L\to M$ be an arbitrary actual module map. Put $I=\operatorname{im}u$ in the abelian category of $\Lambda_S$-modules. Then the actual restriction
$$R\Gamma(T,J I[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma(T_0,t^*J I[0])$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$, naturally for squares of such maps $u$. No finite-model, constructibility, closed-image or completeness assertion about $I$ is made. In free coordinates on weakly contractible covers the maps are allowed continuous matrices on the profinite component space, and are not required to be locally constant matrices. The hypothesis $\mathsf B_\Lambda(t)$ is supplied independently, not concluded by this assertion; for $u=\mathrm{id}_L$ its conclusion is already one of the supplied hypotheses. The original locally torsion étale cohomology comparison remains a hypothesis. Empty schemes, zero modules, the zero coefficient ring and the identity chain are included.

proof.text: Apply the closed-restriction operations lemma to the given closed immersion and pulled-back coefficient ring. Its functors are exactly $\Phi(K)=R\Gamma(T,K)$ and $\Psi(K)=R\Gamma(T_0,t^*K)$, and its transformation $\rho$ is the actual module-derived restriction in the statement. In particular it supplies a morphism of distinguished triangles, including the connecting square; no preservation of injectives by $t^*$ is needed. Let $\mathcal E$ be the full replete class of $K\in D(\mathcal A_T)$ for which $\rho_K$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Refinement proof (2), closed-fibre heart-comparison prerequisite: agent assembly of the supplied finite-model comparisons.

proof.text: The class $\mathcal E$ contains zero, since both functors are additive. The shift compatibility supplied in step 1 makes it closed under every integer shift. For a distinguished triangle with two vertices in $\mathcal E$, the morphism of triangles of step 1 and the triangle two-out-of-three lemma put the third vertex in $\mathcal E$. It is also closed under retracts: for $K\xrightarrow{i}L\xrightarrow{p}K$ with $pi=1$ and $L\in\mathcal E$, an inverse to $\rho_K$ is $\Phi(p)\rho_L^{-1}\Psi(i)$. Naturality gives $\rho_K\Phi(p)\rho_L^{-1}\Psi(i)=\Psi(pi)=1$ and $\Phi(p)\rho_L^{-1}\Psi(i)\rho_K=\Phi(pi)=1$.

source.place: Refinement proof (2), closed-fibre heart-comparison prerequisite: agent assembly of the supplied finite-model comparisons.

proof.text: For a small family in $\mathcal E$, the projection comparisons in the operations lemma identify restriction on its derived product with the product of the invertible restrictions; the inverse is the product of the inverses. For a strict small filtered diagram of complexes with a common termwise lower bound whose derived objects lie in $\mathcal E$, the same lemma identifies restriction on the termwise colimit with the filtered colimit of the restrictions. The inverses form a natural transformation as well (invert the naturality squares), hence give an inverse on that colimit. Thus $\mathcal E$ has exactly both infinite-operation closure properties required in the definition of $\mathcal G_T$ in the generation lemma. Both $T$ and $T_0$ are qcqs, as required for the filtered comparisons; no condition on the complement of $t$ has been inserted.

source.place: Refinement proof (2), closed-fibre heart-comparison prerequisite: agent assembly of the supplied finite-model comparisons.

proof.text: The separately supplied hypothesis $\mathsf B_\Lambda(t)$ says that $JL[0]\in\mathcal E$ for every admissible support chain rooted in $T$ and every finite scalar local model on its source. Together with steps 2--3 this makes $\mathcal E$ one of the classes intersected to define $\mathcal G_T$, so $\mathcal G_T\subseteq\mathcal E$ by the definition of intersection. The structural generation lemma applies to the chosen chain and actual map $u:L\to M$: its coefficients, scalar-model definition, allowed covers and support arrows are the same, including all-continuous $\Omega$ coefficients. It yields $J(\operatorname{im}u)[0]\in\mathcal G_T$. Therefore $\rho_{J(\operatorname{im}u)[0]}$ is invertible, which is exactly the claimed arrow in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. The original torsion comparison remains a hypothesis; the proof uses the independently supplied $\mathsf B_\Lambda(t)$ and does not derive it.

source.place: Refinement proof (2), closed-fibre heart-comparison prerequisite: agent assembly of the supplied finite-model comparisons.

proof.text: For a square of module maps, the composites into the second target agree, so the image factorization induces its map between the two image subobjects; this follows from the universal image factorization and is compatible with composition of squares. Apply $J$ and the natural transformation $\rho$ from step 1 to this map to obtain the required naturality square. The generation input and the operations input both allow the identity chain and zero objects. For an identity map its image is the given local model; for a zero map its image is zero. The zero ring and empty schemes are included in those inputs, so none of these cases was removed by the assembly.
